manifest.title: Kepler-8 b: The Repeating Transit
manifest.subtitle: Observed NASA Kepler Quarter 1 photometry of confirmed exoplanet Kepler-8 b
preparationSteps: Retrieved primary science product from STScI Mikulski Archive (MAST)
Extracted PDCSAP_FLUX and filtered to SAP_QUALITY == 0
manifest.attribution: NASA Kepler Science Mission / STScI MAST Archive
manifest.reuseNotes: Public domain NASA astronomical archive data.

teaching.learningGoal: Discover and align a repeating periodic transit in authentic NASA space telescope data.
teaching.skillPracticed: Phase folding, period fitting, and repetition verification
guidedQuestions: When you adjust the trial period near 3.52 days, what happens to the scattered dips in the phase plot?
How many distinct transit events occurred during this 33-day observation period?
Does an aligned dip prove the presence of an exoplanet by itself, or could a binary star create this?
teaching.explanationSummary: Kepler-8 b is a hot Jupiter exoplanet orbiting an F-type star with an orbital period of approximately 3.5225 days. The transit depth is approximately 0.93% (9,300 ppm) with a duration of ~3.2 hours.

teacherAnswerReveal.astronomicalContext: Discovered by the Kepler space telescope in 2010 (Jenkins et al. 2010).
teacherAnswerReveal.trueNature: Confirmed hot Jupiter gas giant exoplanet
teacherAnswerReveal.evidenceEvaluation: Shows 9 distinct, evenly-spaced transits with identical depths. No secondary eclipse is visible in optical light at phase 0.5. Odd and even transit depths are consistent within observational error.
alternativeExplanations: Eclipsing binary with identical components (ruled out by radial velocity confirmation).
Background blended binary (ruled out by high-resolution imaging and centroid analysis).
